program.title: Deliver a governed and recoverable institutional repository beta
program.outcome: Meet the lab/project repository promise within an explicitly accepted institutional scope.
program.completion: All required items pass with retained evidence and named acceptance; SITE01 adds C01/W03 as blocking dependencies when the selected beta needs them. No production cutover or implementation completion is implied by planning.

items.title: Define institutional beta scope, owners and acceptance envelope
items.ownerRole: Product owner with institutional operator and curator
items.outcome: A named deployment brief replacing planning assumptions with the selected institution's actual needs.
acceptance: Record hosting, identity provider and external-collaborator model, data classification, permitted source collections, retention/withdrawal obligations and support hours.
Name acceptance owners and record capacity, growth, availability and recovery targets, distinguishing scientific-data RPO from restrictive-policy durability.

Explicitly reconcile beta scope with PRD targets and original pilot gates; if DICOM/XNAT or visualization is essential, make C01/W03 a dependency of program completion. Unavailable real inputs remain open; do not invent acceptance.

items.title: Specify lab, project, role and offboarding contracts
items.outcome: A small organizational model with explicit authority and a migration path from the existing curator model.
acceptance: Write an ADR and role/action matrix covering lab membership, project participation, dataset placement, discovery, source evidence, fixed-release sharing, grant expiry, principal disablement and stewardship transfer.
Define link-versus-authority behavior, independent versus membership-derived grants and last-steward recovery without rewriting scientific identities.
Specify public API and migration examples for existing datasets/curators; keep proposals clear where institution-specific inputs are outstanding.

items.title: Persist governed labs, projects and memberships
items.outcome: Reference and PostgreSQL catalogs support durable organizational records and controlled administration.
acceptance: Add checked migrations and application contracts for labs/projects, membership, project dataset placement and human-readable metadata; preserve existing release IDs and attribution.
Migrate old curator/dataset records explicitly and provide audited stewardship transfer; no default public workspace or accidental access widening.
Prove reference/PostgreSQL agreement, concurrent updates, authorized administration, upgrade preservation and denial of unauthorized membership changes.

items.title: Enforce current memberships, principal state and expiring access
items.outcome: Every repository access path reflects current organizational authority, with explainable effective access.
acceptance: Replace permanent curator bypass with governed stewardship and enforce principal disablement, membership removal and grant expiry transactionally.

Apply authority to directory listings/counts, dataset/release reads, queries, preparations, acceptance/retries/receipts, downloads and run input/destination use; preserve bounded disclosure and fixed-release semantics.

Add authorized effective-access inspection and negative fixtures for cross-lab leakage, independent grants, concurrent policy changes and stale contexts; ensure continuing delivery rechecks the declared policy bound.

items.title: Implement institutional sign-in and browser-session lifecycle
items.outcome: One institutional identity provider authenticates stable principals with a usable and revocable browser session.
acceptance: Use verified provider subject bindings; cover approved external collaborators, account disablement/recovery, expiry and logout without email-only identity merging.
Define session storage/transport, origin and request protections, secret rotation and current authorization; retain explicit service credentials rather than conferring arbitrary caller identity.

Qualify provider errors, invalid/stale sessions and contract behavior in automated fixtures; retain a selected-provider staging rehearsal before beta qualification. Missing real provider access stays an explicit open gate.

items.title: Deliver authorized lab and project discovery in the console
items.outcome: A signed-in user finds permitted projects/datasets and manages collaboration without typing internal IDs.
acceptance: Implement bounded authorized directory/search APIs and console navigation from login through lab/project/dataset to existing release and curation screens.
Provide human-readable collaborator selection, effective-access explanation, scope/future-release distinction, expiry and revocation under the same backend contracts.
Include empty/denied/error/stale-session states, keyboard/focus behavior and leakage checks for titles, counts and suggestions; do not duplicate authority rules in the browser.

items.title: Qualify the two-lab institutional foundation journey
items.outcome: A retained end-to-end demonstration of sign-in, organization, sharing and offboarding across two labs.
acceptance: Exercise real browser/HTTP/PostgreSQL with two labs, reader/contributor/steward roles, one external collaborator and a migrated preexisting dataset.
Demonstrate denied discovery, sharing/revocation, membership removal, principal disablement, concurrent role changes and stewardship handover while preserving historical releases and attribution.
Retain source-bound automated and human workflow/accessibility evidence with explicit not-run provider or screen-reader gates; completion of this tranche does not assert institutional readiness.

items.title: Package an installable service with controlled upgrades
items.outcome: A clean institutional staging host can run a pinned Sanctity release without using sbt as the service manager.
acceptance: Supply a versioned artifact/deployment manifest, validated configuration, TLS/origin and secret setup, process supervision and graceful shutdown.
Separate migration privileges/command from runtime database access; retain drift checks and provide upgrade failure/restore procedures and compatibility checks for old releases.
Rehearse clean installation and an upgrade from the existing schema with pinned sources/dependencies and retained results; do not claim hosted CI or deployment execution without receipts.

items.title: Make service health, storage limits and failures observable
items.outcome: Operators see and can respond to resource exhaustion, failed work and unavailable dependencies before data stewardship fails.
acceptance: Provide distinct liveness/readiness including the closed recovery gate, redacted structured diagnostics, authorized audit inspection, useful metrics and tested alert delivery.
Account for accepted/staged/abandoned/backup storage; enforce capacity reservations and bounded queues/concurrency, including streaming response lifetimes and large inventory responses.

Exercise database outage, disk-full, failed/abandoned imports and cancellation; document escalation, safe service behavior and integrity scrub/repair procedures without enabling unqualified garbage collection.

items.title: Preserve current authority independently and automate disaster recovery
items.outcome: Catalog/blob loss cannot force recovery to trust stale permissions or credentials.
acceptance: Design and implement an independently durable authority journal/checkpoint with sequence/completeness and authenticity verification, including memberships, stewardship and principal disablement; specify restrictive-change acknowledgment and replication-failure behavior.

Schedule verified off-host catalog/blob backups and rehearse restore with the source database unavailable; reconcile current policy, invalidate old credentials/sessions/leases and remain closed when evidence is incomplete.
Measure backup age/RPO and catalog/API versus full-blob-loss RTO; retain verifiable backup and recovery receipts. A digest or copy on the original host alone is insufficient.

items.title: Enforce quarantine, withdrawal and recovery lifecycle policy
items.ownerRole: Backend engineer with institutional data steward
items.outcome: Withdrawal and any required erasure have explicit effects on current service and restored copies.
acceptance: Implement durable quarantine/withdrawal controls and journal them independently; define current delivery, linked views, pending operations and derivative obligations without inferring permissions from provenance.
Document institution-specific retention, backup expiry, shared-blob reachability and any required physical-erasure procedure; keep automatic collection disabled unless separately qualified.

Back up, then withdraw/restrict data, lose the original host and restore: restricted content remains unavailable. Required erasure or source-evidence obligations that lack a qualified procedure block admission of affected data.

items.title: Complete authenticated intake and reproducible export workflows
items.outcome: Curators can create and populate a dataset and researchers can obtain verified full exports through supported product workflows.
acceptance: Expose authorized creation, approved staging intake and/or bounded resumable upload through durable operation contracts, with quotas and source-evidence isolation; reject arbitrary server paths.
Show scope, findings, progress and supported retry/cancel/resume actions; preserve atomic publication and allow mapping/metadata decisions without database edits.
Provide durable full-export planning, progress, verified delivery and interruption recovery under current authority; demonstrate complete browser/API journeys on supported native BIDS.

items.title: Add project curation, release history and review work
items.outcome: A project shows its datasets, responsibilities and outstanding review work in one coherent workflow.
acceptance: Provide project overview, authorized dataset search and bounded inventory/history navigation, assignment/status/notes for curation tasks, and an activity trail.
Bind findings, reports and human review outcomes to exact releases; distinguish acceptance, automated checks and reviewed quality; new releases do not silently inherit approval.
Keep task/attachment/search visibility within underlying dataset authority; curator and researcher complete daily work without operator CLI or internal UUID entry.

items.title: Integrate bounded image or QA report inspection when required
items.outcome: A selected visualization workflow consumes existing versioned data or reports through normal access contracts.
acceptance: Choose one concrete review need with pilot users and integrate an existing viewer/report surface; do not add another numerical recipe.
Preserve exact release/result lineage and current authority on previews, thumbnails, caching and reports; isolate untrusted report content.
Qualify accessibility and realistic payload/resource behavior. SITE01 makes this a launch dependency only if the chosen beta requires it; otherwise retain as later work.

items.title: Qualify representative data and the institutional capacity envelope
items.ownerRole: Backend engineer with scientist and operator
items.outcome: A published supported envelope describes measured capacity and correct behavior on representative institutional data.
acceptance: Use named permitted collections and independent expected results for import, curation, query, exact historical export and accounting; honor source/scientific support boundaries.

Measure realistic grants, concurrent readers/imports, large files, many files, revision growth, memory, latency and throughput; qualify pagination and the existing 10000-entry ceiling before enlarging it.
Retain workload/hardware/source identities and raw results; explicitly resolve applicable PRD targets or approved narrower beta scope rather than treating small fixture timings as an SLA.

items.title: Close access review and human usability adoption gates
items.outcome: The institutional collaboration and interface claims have independent and human acceptance evidence.
acceptance: Review and exercise current role/action boundaries, denied discovery/counts, session/grant expiry, revocation, restricted source/report leakage and selected browser-session protections.
Have representative curators/researchers complete import, organization, correction/conflict recovery, sharing and retrieval; resolve blocking findings.

Complete actual screen-reader/keyboard evidence including CON-03; record reviewer, versions, source state, outcomes and unresolved limitations. Automated checks cannot stand in for missing human results.

items.title: Rehearse clean-host recovery and institutional operator handover
items.outcome: An operator can own a bounded institutional beta and recover it without the original engineer or server.
acceptance: A different operator installs/upgrades the packaged release, diagnoses an injected fault and restores onto replacement infrastructure using the documented independent backup/policy sources.
Revoke access and withdraw data after backup, then lose the original host; verify current restrictions, exact retained exports and coherent pending work after recovery; meet accepted RPO/RTO.

Verify real alert/escalation delivery and support responsibilities, record beta observation criteria and runbook results, and identify any conditional source/visualization gate. Production cutover requires a separate service-owner decision.

items.title: Qualify the selected DICOM or XNAT source when adoption requires it
items.outcome: Only the advertised source installation and acquisition profiles are claimed as qualified.
acceptance: Survey the named XNAT installation/resources and/or DICOM collection, preserve restricted evidence, specify mappings and independent scientific fixtures, and record exclusions.
Rehearse interruption, source/output accounting and final reconciliation with the real permitted collection; conversion success alone is insufficient.
When SITE01 selects this source for beta, make this item a blocking program dependency; otherwise keep it distinct from native-BIDS beta and retain original migration-pilot obligations.
